title: Probabilistic TTL + Shadow Eviction Validation for Prefix-Safe KV Cache
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Investigate and implement a probabilistic TTL estimator combined with a shadow-mode eviction validator to ensure prefix-aware correctness while respecting strict GPU memory budgets. Continuous batching interacts with KV caching and GPU allocation in ways that make deterministic LRU unsafe for some workloads (partial-prefix evictions, asynchronous writebacks, and race windows between eviction and batch replay). This ticket designs the policy, implements a non-disruptive shadow validation harness in production, and lands safety guards (atomic prefix tombstones + epoching) with GPU memory accounting hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow-mode can run on 5% of traffic without altering live responses and produce daily correctness diff reports
Probabilistic TTL estimator reduces steady-state cache eviction-induced generation regressions by >= 60% on internal replay tests
Atomic prefix tombstone + epoch protocol prevents any observed partial-prefix read-after-evict correctness regressions in 10k synthetic scenario runs
GPU allocator exposes per-prefix peak and resident accounting metrics and stays within budget during 99th percentile batching workloads
Integration tests (unit, integration, e2e) and a canary rollout plan documented and approved by SRE
implementation_notes: Add a lightweight probabilistic TTL counter per prefix using decay window counters instead of strong per-key timers to save memory
Introduce 'shadow-evict' mode in runtime that records what would have been evicted by new policy and compares to actual policy without modifying KV state
Implement atomic prefix tombstones: write tombstone marker plus epoch increment in a single durable op; readers check epoch to reject stale KV entries
GPU memory accounting: hook into CUDA allocator to tag allocations with prefix-id and record resident set sizes per-prefix; report to /metrics and Console
Expose a 'safe-evict' API used by Dedicated/Private to respect customer pinning and cross-check with release policies
Integrate with continuous batching: eviction scheduler will consult batch-in-flight tracker to avoid evicting prefixes referenced by active batches
Performance: keep per-request overhead under 1% tail latency impact when shadow-mode enabled; sample only a fraction of requests if necessary
Fallbacks: on detection of disagreement where shadow-policy would have caused incorrect behavior, auto-roll back new policy and notify on-call with traces and sample payloads

risks: Sampling false negatives during shadow-mode (rare disagreements not exercised by sample traffic) — mitigated by offline replay and randomized stress runs
GPU accounting overhead could increase allocation latency — mitigated by tag-on-alloc design and batched metrics export
Interactions with Dedicated autoscaler: eviction policy may conflict with reserved pool assumptions — mitigation: feature flag per-deployment and opt-in testing
Long TTLs in probabilistic estimator could cause memory bloat for low-throughput prefixes — mitigation: combine with LRU for low-activity eviction tier
